items.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Because I had gone through a lot of influences since then, it’s like a recipe, you know you take a little bit of Red Garland, a little bit or Horace Silver, a little bit of George Wallington, a little bit of Bud, a little bit of Bill Evans, whatever.

ctx.x: Do you feel that you have influenced any people yourself? Some of the younger players? Frank Zappa maybe?

You know that’s a good question and it’s a difficult one for me to answer because there have been times when I’ve listened to somebody and because I know when I hear myself immediately that it’s me. Because what you just played me, I don’t play that way anymore. You know what I mean? I mean I know that when I hear back on a piano playing I know that that goes way back. That was in my twenties. Because I had gone through a lot of influences since then, it’s like a recipe, you know you take a little bit of Red…
left, I’m thinking of some of those things Zoot played on the sax. And that’s really where I’m coming from.
